name: HMS Hood — 1941 battle fit
axes: right-handed: X bow-positive; Y up; Z transverse
configuration: Hood 1941 demonstration fit: eight 15-inch guns, seven twin 4-inch mounts, three octuple 2-pounders and four quadruple 0.5-inch mounts. Superseded 5.5-inch guns removed. UP launcher assemblies and exact refit small details are not modeled.
accuracy: Major equipment stations reviewed against the identified recognition plan. Longitudinal coordinates are measured proportions of that ship drawing, not shipyard frame offsets. Hull body sections, turret casings, bridge details, small fittings and underwater surfaces remain inferred exterior artwork. Campaign secondary counts are retained where the catalog differs from the illustrated refit. No claim of a survey-accurate or exact individual wartime refit. The primary profile informs the taller conning/bridge complex and extended shelter/boat deck; minor 1941 platform dimensions and deckhouse details remain inferred.
geometrySource: New curved hull, deck and detailed fittings authored independently. The earlier recognition station ledger supplies locations and equipment counts only; no earlier vertices, faces, surface shapes or colors are imported.

sources.title: Brassey's Naval and Shipping Annual 1923, plate 1 (PDF page 489)
sources.license: Public domain in the United States (published 1923)
sources.usedFor: Identity, configuration, recorded longitudinal equipment layout and recognition outline; new curved surfaces and small fittings are original inferred exterior reconstruction.

sources.title: WNT1922 campaign catalog
sources.usedFor: Class dimensions, armament, propulsion and complement.

sources.title: HMS Hood Association secondary guns, citing Priddys Hard gun records
sources.usedFor: Seven twin 4-inch mounts: three per side plus one after shelter-deck centerline. Removal of all 5.5-inch guns by May 1940.

sources.title: HMS Hood Association anti-aircraft fit record
sources.usedFor: Three octuple pom-poms, four quadruple Vickers mounts, and general forward/after shelter-deck distribution.

layoutProvenance: Independent station review, 2026-09-30; preserved class recognition reference in sources. Hood Brassey plan: two funnels, four twins, both inner turrets raised. Main turret centers and masts measured from this vessel plan, rather than a generic capital-ship layout. Hood same-hull derivative with independently declared 1941 weapons; no unrelated class geometry substituted.
